bull_bear.body:
- Debt-free (net D/E -0.4); FY26 cash flow = 58% of EBITDA after capex. ROCE 94%.
- Reinvesting into two greenfields (~INR140 cr) while keeping balance-sheet flexibility; open to M&A for margin-accretive entry into new segments. No dividend policy detail this call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Clean Air growth tepid (+5.5% FY26):** vehicle-mix dependent (low-end vs high-end SUV mix within OEMs; one European OEM shifting to EVs) — mgmt insists no competitive share loss; recovery hinges on #1-OEM panel entry (FY28) and CAFE/BS7 content.
- **Absent from India's #1 PV OEM until FY28:** missed GST-benefit-driven volume at that OEM in FY26.
- **EV adoption** (full-EV eliminates exhaust content) — partly mitigated by global hybrid/range-extender swing-back.
- **Indirect-cost inflation & FX:** freight (Middle-East war), plastics/rubber, LPG/CNG/crude, currency — recovery requires "tough discussions" with OEMs; not all caused by company.
- **One-time labour-code charge** dented FY26 PAT; watch recurrence/quantum.
- **Execution/commissioning slippage** on the two new plants and the middle-ended export ramp (peak ~2028-29).
- **Disclosure gaps:** bearings order value, labour-code charge quantum, exact export-mix path not quantified.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - CEO Arvind highly articulate, technology-led, candid on the Clean Air mix softness ("not share loss") and on cost-recovery friction. Confident/promotional on DaVinci DCx ("total game changer," "don't take my word — check YouTube/Instagram") but grounds it in OEM traction and the Mahindra 7XO. CFO disciplined, KPI-led (VAR, ROCE, cash conversion). Consistent narrative thread to IPO roadshow (P3, Lego-brick model, localization). Margin-disciplined — explicitly won't chase low-margin 2W/3W just for volume.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The EV-slowdown is a *positive* for this name: hybrids/range-extenders keep — and can raise (X→1.5-2X via acoustic valves) — Clean Air content, inverting the usual auto-component EV-disruption fear.
- DaVinci DCx is a deliberate "good-enough mechanical" disruptor positioned *below* electronic semi-active (CVSA) — captures the mass mid-premium SUV (<INR35 lakh) where 90% of India still runs single-tuning legacy dampers; the affordability/no-electronics angle is the moat vs both legacy shock-absorber makers and costly electronic suspension.
- The reported Clean Air weakness is a *mix optics* problem, not demand/share — the real inflection is contractual: #1-OEM GPF panel entry (FY28) + INR1,300-1,400 cr CAFE-3/BS7 content window.
- Rupee depreciation is net-accretive (90% localized) and is itself an export growth engine (~15-20% competitiveness) — currency is a tailwind, not a risk, for this localized exporter.
- 94% ROCE + negative cash-conversion-cycle + 1:3 capex-to-revenue = an unusually capital-light, high-return auto-component compounder.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on the Tenneco Group and the risk of adverse changes in key relationships (strategic risk) — The Company derives significant strategic and operational benefits from its association with the Tenneco Group through access to its technology platforms, intellectual property and operational processes. An adverse change in these arrangements or relationships could impact competitiveness, technology access, operational continuity and future growth visibility across businesses. Mitigation is close alignment with the Group across engineering, manufacturing and operational excellence, while strengthening local execution capability and localisation.
- Revenue concentration across top customers (strategic risk) — A significant share of revenues comes from a limited number of OEM customers, so customer sourcing decisions, platform allocations, production schedules and commercial arrangements drive programme visibility. Changes in sourcing strategies, production volumes, pricing arrangements or platform mix by key customers may impact revenue concentration, operating performance and medium-term growth visibility. Mitigation is customer stickiness via early lifecycle engagement, a technology-intensive portfolio with rigorous validation and long programme lifecycles, and expansion across domestic and export programmes. The social capital section separately acknowledges customer concentration and supply-chain reliance as inherent stakeholder-dependency risks.
- Revenue concentration in the passenger vehicle and commercial vehicle segments (strategic risk) — A significant portion of revenues is linked to PV and CV segments, whose demand depends on economic activity, infrastructure spending, freight movement, fuel prices, financing availability and consumer sentiment. A prolonged slowdown in vehicle production or lower industry demand could impact revenues, operating leverage and profitability. Mitigation is portfolio diversification across Clean Air, Champion Ignition, Powertrain and Advanced Ride Technologies, plus increasing participation in industrial and off-highway platforms and export programmes.
- Lack of firm volume commitments from customers (operational risk) — OEM production schedules and order volumes are based on customer forecasts and market demand, so order visibility is subject to changes in production schedules, inventory levels and industry demand. The absence of firm long-term volume commitments may impact production planning, capacity utilisation, inventory management and operational efficiency across facilities. Mitigation is operational flexibility from a diversified programme portfolio and disciplined capacity planning, and closer work with customers on forecasting visibility. This is a structural qualifier on the disclosed order book.
- Dependence on government emission standards and their implementation timelines (technological / regulatory risk) — Demand for several products, particularly Clean Air and emission-control systems, is linked to evolving emission regulations and compliance requirements. Delays, modifications or changes in emission standards and implementation timelines could influence product demand, programme timing, investment cycles and technology adoption across vehicle platforms. Mitigation is aligning engineering, product development and manufacturing readiness with evolving emission norms while leveraging global technology platforms and localisation. The MD&A separately notes that lower-horsepower (<75 Hp) tractor engine emission regulations were deferred to 2032, an example of exactly this timing risk crystallising.
- Raw material price and availability risk, including steel and precious metals (operational risk) — The Company is exposed to fluctuations in prices and availability of key raw materials and components including steel, precious metals and commodity-linked inputs. Sustained commodity price increases and supply bottlenecks across critical materials may impact margins, production continuity, working capital requirements and cost competitiveness. Mitigation is supplier diversification, strategic sourcing, inventory planning, cost optimisation and customer pass-through arrangements where applicable, supported by localisation.
- Dynamic geopolitical conditions, trade restrictions and tariff actions (strategic risk) — Geopolitical uncertainty, trade restrictions, tariff actions, regional conflicts and supply-chain realignments may affect raw material availability, energy costs and reliability, logistics networks, exports, commodity prices and customer production schedules. Sustained disruption may influence sourcing continuity, input costs, export competitiveness and demand visibility; changes in trade regulations and tariff structures may also affect cross-border supply chains and intercompany operations. Mitigation includes localisation, diversified supplier relationships, disciplined inventory planning, operational flexibility, diversification of energy sources and energy efficiency initiatives.
- Supply chain dependence and supplier instability (BRSR material issue) — Dependence on supplier networks is critical for uninterrupted production; disruptions from supplier instability may affect production timelines and lead to cost escalations. Mitigation is robust sourcing practices, comprehensive supplier qualification and review frameworks, diversified and dual-sourced procurement, supplier localisation, continuous engagement and transparent governance.
- Information management and cyber security (technological risk) — Data security threats include cyberattacks, data breaches and unauthorised access to sensitive company information. Production schedules may be disrupted, potentially delaying manufacturing processes, impacting delivery timelines and leading to possible regulatory implications. Mitigation is a comprehensive IT and Information Security policy aligned with legal and regulatory requirements.
- Product quality and safety liability (BRSR material issue - risk and opportunity) — In a highly quality-sensitive automotive sector, product defects can directly impact vehicle safety and customer trust; failure to maintain stringent quality standards may result in recalls, warranty claims and loss of OEM relationships. Mitigation is globally aligned quality management systems, 100% IATF 16949 and ISO 9001 certification across the Company's four manufacturing facilities, a 'first-time-right' approach and close OEM collaboration across the product lifecycle.
- Occupational health and safety in manufacturing operations (BRSR material issue) — Operations involve exposure to machinery, high temperatures and industrial processes; ineffective safety management may cause workplace incidents leading to injuries, regulatory action, operational disruption, financial penalties, higher insurance costs and reputational damage. Mitigation is anchored in the global EHS Policy, ISO 45001:2018 and the P3 Operating Standard, with facilities certified to ISO 45001 and ISO 14001 and periodic internal and external audits.
- Human capital - attrition and skill availability (BRSR material issue) — High employee turnover, skill shortages or low engagement can adversely affect productivity and operational performance. This is a live exposure rather than a theoretical one: the BRSR reports a permanent-employee turnover rate of 20.44% in FY 2025-26 (23.34% in FY 2024-25, 22.97% in FY 2023-24), against a permanent-worker turnover rate of 0.50%. Mitigation is structured training, mandatory safety inductions and refresher training, and leadership development through Tenneco University (Tenn U) and the Emerging Leaders Program.
- Business ethics, bribery and corruption exposure (BRSR material issue) — Any breach of ethical standards can lead to legal action, financial penalties and reputational damage. Mitigation is a zero-tolerance approach anchored in the Tenneco Code of Conduct, an anti-corruption framework and regular digital and in-person training. The AR reports NIL bribery/corruption charges against the Board, KMPs, employees and workers, and states that no law enforcement agency has initiated disciplinary action on such charges.

business.body: The Company designs, manufactures and supplies exhaust after-treatment and clean air systems (catalytic converters, DPFs, SCRs, mufflers, exhaust pipes), powertrain products (engine bearings, sealing systems, ignition products) and advanced ride products (shock absorbers, struts, suspension systems) to automotive OEMs and the aftermarket. It operates through two segments - Clean Air & Powertrain Solutions and Advanced Ride Technologies - serving passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles (commercial trucks and off-highway) and industrial/other applications, and sells aftermarket products under the Champion (sparkplugs) and Monroe (suspension) brands. Incorporated in December 2018, the Clean Air business was acquired in 2019 under a Scheme of Arrangement for demerger; the Company converted to a public limited company in May 2025 and listed on BSE and NSE on November 19, 2025.

- 18.8% FY26 EBITDA margin = highest ever, +21bps YoY (14.3% FY24 → 18.8% FY26). Drivers: P3 operating model (People/Performance/Pride), better fixed-cost absorption, disciplined commercial recoveries, "Lego-brick" standardized/modular high-speed canning lines (multi-product per line, pre-validated → high utilization, fast time-to-market, high ROCE).

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this):** Best-ever year — FY26 VAR INR4,918 cr (+12.3%), record 18.8% EBITDA margin, PAT INR604.4 cr (+9.3%, dented by one-time labour-code charge); ROCE 94% (vs 57%), debt-free, lifetime order book INR12,400 cr (100% FY28 visibility). outlook.body:
- 'No Boundaries' is the stated current phase of the Company's evolution, following 'Execute to Win' (establishing discipline) and 'Game On' (raising the bar); management defines it as no ceiling on growth, no tolerance for underperformance and no hesitation in pursuing global programs or first-in-world technologies.
- Run the business on the global P3 (People, Performance, Pride) operating model - a standardised operating framework for plants, programs and processes, institutionalising practices across safety, quality, delivery, cost and continuous improvement.
- Focus on improving content per vehicle, expanding export opportunities, strengthening localisation, enhancing technology intensity across the portfolio and maintaining disciplined execution across the organisation.
- Participate across multiple areas of the automotive value chain through the portfolio spanning Clean Air, Powertrain (Bearings, Sealings & Ignitions) and Advanced Ride Technologies - described as two high-performing growth engines: Clean Air & Powertrain Solutions and Advanced Ride Technologies.
- Build manufacturing proximity to OEM clusters in the north and west of India through the new North India Clean Air facility and the greenfield Western India Advanced Ride Technologies facility, supporting awarded programs across light vehicles, off-highway and tractor segments.
- Position technology as the competitive moat: a global R&D backbone translated locally through two in-house technical centres in India developing solutions tailored to Indian road conditions, cost realities and OEM timelines - evidenced by the patented DaVinci DCx, the Euro VII proof-of-concept and the Toyota Zero-Defect Supplier Award.
- Expand exports and integrate into global OEM sourcing programmes, using Euro VII readiness and entry into the hot end of after-treatment for a leading Japanese PV OEM as the opening for a significantly expanded domestic and export opportunity.
- Build leaders from within through a deliberate architecture of leadership programmes - the first Tenneco University Global Campus hosted in Hyderabad in March 2026, the Emerging Leaders Programme India cohort graduating in February 2026, and participation in the global NextUp Plant Leadership Development Programme.
- Treat safety as the non-negotiable first priority and the first metric reviewed in every operational discussion, deployed through the PARIVARTAN programme across sites.
- Strengthen governance disciplines as a newly listed company, with Board and Committee oversight across strategy, risk, compliance, internal controls and operational performance, supported by whistleblower and vigil mechanisms.
- Management states its competitive advantage comes from culture, parentage, technology, market position, operating model, customer relationships, strong financials and a diverse leadership team.
- No change in the nature of business of the Company during the year under review; the subsidiary structure remained unchanged with no addition or cessation of any subsidiary.
- The Board has formulated a Dividend Distribution Policy pursuant to Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations, available on the Company's website. Four interim dividends were declared and paid during FY 2025-26 (per-share and aggregate amounts are stated in the Directors' Report but are deliberately not reproduced here, since this field is for policy intent rather than figures); all four were declared between April and August 2025, i.e. before the November 2025 listing. No final dividend has been recommended for the financial year ended March 31, 2026: the Board considered it prudent not to do so 'in view of the Company's growth strategy with respect to investments in capacity expansion, technology development, localisation initiatives and other business opportunities', a decision stated to be in line with the Dividend Distribution Policy. Consequently no record date has been fixed for dividend entitlement. The stated reinvestment intent is therefore to retain earnings for capacity expansion, technology development and localisation. Management separately describes the balance sheet qualitatively as very strong with zero net debt, and states that the IPO listing enhances financial flexibility and access to diverse funding avenues and capital markets, supporting strategic expansion. The IPO itself was entirely an Offer for Sale by the promoter selling shareholder, so no primary proceeds accrued to the Company.
- Roadmap stated to be technology ready to meet the upcoming BS VII / CAFE regulations in the next 3-5 years - the single explicitly time-bound ESG-linked target in the routed text (BRSR material issue 'Carbon Emissions', classified as an Opportunity with positive financial implications).
- All four of the Company's manufacturing facilities have achieved 100% certification under IATF 16949 and ISO 9001 (product quality and safety).
- Manufacturing facilities are certified to ISO 45001 (occupational health and safety, ISO 45001:2018) and ISO 14001 (environmental management), with systematic risk assessment and periodic internal and external audits.
- ESG governance architecture: the CEO oversees the Company's ESG strategy and reporting; the Risk Management Committee reviews and mitigates sustainability-related risks including ESG risks; the Board provides ultimate oversight. The Risk Management Committee, Audit Committee and Board are all chaired by Independent Directors, and the Risk Management Committee currently meets twice during the year.
- Materiality assessment completed, aligned with leading international frameworks, identifying material topics across Environment (Carbon Emissions, Renewable Energy), Social (Product Quality and Safety, Occupational Health and Safety, Human Capital, Supply Chain Management) and Governance (Corporate Governance, Business Ethics, Risk Management). Renewable Energy is named as a material topic but no renewable-energy target or figure appears in the routed text.
- Eight material responsible business conduct issues are disclosed with rationale, mitigation and the direction of financial implication: Product Quality and Safety (positive and negative), Carbon Emissions (positive), Occupational Health and Safety (positive and negative), Corporate Governance (positive and negative), Business Ethics and Conduct (negative), Risk Management (negative), Human Capital (positive and negative), Supply Chain Management (negative).
- 'Speak Up' culture supported by the Tenneco Ethics & Compliance Hotline - an independent, 24/7 reporting mechanism offering anonymity where permitted by law and protection against retaliation; all concerns reviewed and investigated confidentially through defined governance and remediation processes.
- Stakeholder complaints in FY 2025-26 with none pending at year-end in any category: Shareholders 165 complaints filed (nil in FY 2024-25 - the Company listed only in November 2025), Employees and workers 14 (1 in FY 2024-25), Customers 1 (nil), Others 4 anonymous whistleblower complaints (2 in FY 2024-25); Communities, Investors (other than shareholders) and Value Chain Partners recorded a printed '-' i.e. stated nil.
- Dedicated Investor Grievance Redressal Policy under Regulation 13 of the SEBI LODR: grievances first handled by the Registrar and Transfer Agent (MUFG Intime India Private Limited), escalable to the Compliance Officer and then SEBI SCORES, with a defined 21-calendar-day resolution timeline, a structured escalation matrix and periodic reporting to the Board and stock exchanges.
- NIL bribery / corruption charges against the Board of Directors, KMPs, employees and workers; no law enforcement agency has initiated disciplinary action against any Director, KMP, employee or worker on charges related to bribery or corruption.
- Community/CSR programmes disclosed: an athlete support initiative for talented athletes from underserved communities providing financial assistance, professional coaching, sports infrastructure, healthcare, nutrition and educational continuity (aligned to SDG 3, SDG 10 and SDG 17 and to Khelo India and India's Olympic/Paralympic priorities); health and eye check-up camps; an air purifier programme; and skills/employability programmes. Disclosed beneficiary counts include 151 athletes, 67 para-athletes and 2,205 health-camp beneficiaries.
- Environmental volunteering: planned clean-up drives with Times Employ India Foundation at Chakan (Pune) and Gurugram with 131 'TENN ECO Warriors' participating, collecting and responsibly managing approximately 373 Kg of waste; aligned to SDG 11 and the Swachh Bharat Mission.
- BRSR reporting boundary and assurance context: disclosures are made on a standalone basis, with reasonable assurance on Core parameters provided by Adwin Advisory Services Private Limited (stated in BRSR Section A, routed via the profile/governance prompts).
- Internal controls: an independent internal audit function supported by external audit firms follows a risk-based plan approved by the Audit Committee, with key observations and management action plans reviewed quarterly; the Company states that during the year no material weaknesses in the design or operation of internal financial controls were observed.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Capacity planning is stated to be closely aligned with customer programmes and demand outlook. Two additions are named: a new plant for Clean Air products being added in FY 2026-27 to cater to customers in the North region, and a capacity enhancement at the Chakan Sealings Facility for its products driven by export opportunities. The leadership reflection adds that the North India Clean Air facility was approved earlier in the year with production expected by end-FY 2026-27, and that the Board of the subsidiary has now also approved a greenfield Advanced Ride Technologies manufacturing facility in Western India - taking total announced capacity investment to INR 1,400 Million. Together these facilities are said to strengthen proximity to OEM clusters in the north and west and support awarded programs across light vehicles, off-highway and tractor segments. Beyond the two greenfield projects, the Company describes a network-led approach rather than standalone capacity addition: presence within established industrial clusters supports modular expansion aligned with programme growth, enabling scalability through optimisation and improving capital effectiveness. The multi-location manufacturing network is described as supporting flexible capacity management with dynamic allocation of production loads, inherent redundancy against plant-level disruption, and process/equipment standardisation that allows the Company to flex or transfer equipment and shift products across facilities in alignment with customers. Under the P3 operating framework, P3-certified plants increased from 2 in the previous year to 6 currently, with an additional 4 plants applying for certification in Q1 FY 2026-27, and all 12 plants across Clean Air, Powertrain and Advanced Ride Technologies are stated to have improved on safety, quality, delivery and operating standards aligned to global Tenneco certification levels. Operational performance is tracked through Overall Asset Effectiveness (OAE), direct labour efficiency savings and year-on-year productivity savings. On the input side, 90% of total procurement is sourced locally, the top 10 suppliers contribute 24% of total procurement spend and are dual sourced (described as low supplier concentration risk), and freight rates are fixed through agreements with logistics vendors with vehicles dedicated exclusively to Tenneco. The BRSR states that capex is primarily directed towards upgrading manufacturing facilities with energy-efficient, low-emission technologies and pollution control systems. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum for the year is disclosed anywhere in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Passenger vehicles: the industry is expected to maintain a steady growth trajectory during FY 2026-27, supported by continued premiumisation, new launches, improving rural demand and increasing adoption of alternative fuel technologies; OEM focus on SUVs, hybrids, EVs and feature-led differentiation is expected to remain strong, with stable financing availability and healthier inventory levels supporting demand.
- Passenger vehicle watch-items flagged: fuel prices, affordability pressures, supply-side disruptions, a declining Rupee and regulatory developments; also CNG/hybrid/EV adoption trajectory, SUV demand and premiumisation, consumer sentiment and financing affordability, cost of raw material imports due to the declining Rupee, and inventory discipline and supply availability.
- Commercial vehicles and tractors: expected to witness moderate but healthy growth during FY 2026-27, supported by continued infrastructure investments, freight demand, replacement cycles and stable rural sentiment; LCVs and buses expected to remain relatively resilient, while infrastructure execution, industrial activity, financing conditions and fleet utilisation are likely to influence M&HCV demand.
- Commercial vehicle factors to watch: government infrastructure and capex spending, freight demand and fleet utilisation, rural income and monsoon outlook, fuel prices and financing conditions, replacement demand cycles, and premiumisation driven by driver shortage.
- Off-highway: FY 2025-26 performance was subdued with construction equipment retail volumes declining 11.7% YoY to 71,227 units on project execution delays and a high base; continued investments across roads, railways, logistics corridors, urban infrastructure and core sectors are expected to support a gradual recovery in equipment demand during FY 2026-27, with commodity cycles, execution timelines, export demand and financing availability as key determinants.
- Indian auto component industry: the ACMA-BCG study cites ~14% CAGR over the past five years to nearly USD 80 billion; ACMA studies with McKinsey and BCG project the sector to reach approximately USD 200 billion in revenues by FY 2029-30, with exports alone estimated at USD 70-100 billion.
- Management explicitly cautions that raw material volatility, tariffs, high costs of imports due to a weakening Rupee, and supply constraints from the ongoing mid-east crisis could have a material effect on revenues and margins.
- Exhaust after-treatment demand driver: implementation of BS VI Phase 2 with Real Driving Emissions (RDE) compliance has aligned Indian standards closely with European regulations, significantly increasing technological complexity and value addition in catalytic converters, DPFs and SCR systems; OEMs are increasingly adopting more complex, higher-specification after-treatment solutions to meet CAFE III and future BS VII requirements.
- The clean air solutions segment is projected to grow at an 8-10% CAGR between FY 2024-25 and FY 2029-30, supported by higher precious-metal loadings, advanced catalyst chemistries and increasing localisation of critical components (industry projection cited in the MD&A, illustrated by a chart that is not reproduced in the routed text).
- India's improving technology parity with global emission norms is enabling component suppliers to integrate into global OEM sourcing programmes, positioning India as a competitive export base for after-treatment systems aligned with Euro VI, future Euro VII, CAFE and TREM V standards.
- Tractor regulatory nuance: lower-horsepower engine (<75 Hp) emission regulations were delayed to 2032 while higher-horsepower engine-emission regulations remain in effect for 2026; the delay does not affect Indian OEMs exporting to markets where Trem V or similar norms still apply.
- Suspension and ride performance: demand remained robust in FY 2025-26 on vehicle premiumisation, rising SUV penetration and OEM focus on ride comfort, handling and NVH optimisation, with a gradual shift toward higher-content suspension architectures including passive, semi-active and electronically assisted systems.
- Powertrain (sealings, ignition, bearings): benefits from rising technology content across ICE, alternative-fuel and hybrid powertrains, with stricter CAFE III efficiency norms and OEM efforts to reduce frictional losses, improve thermal efficiency and enhance durability driving demand for advanced materials and precision-engineered components.
- FY 2025-26 domestic demand support: GST rationalisation ('GST 2.0') improved vehicle affordability by reducing effective tax incidence, and together with multiple repo rate cuts and income-tax relief measures helped unlock deferred demand, support replacement cycles and improve financing affordability across urban and rural markets.
- Operating conditions during FY 2025-26 remained influenced by raw material volatility, tariff-related uncertainties, and supply constraints relating to critical materials; geopolitical uncertainties and commodity price volatility remain key monitorables going forward.
- Macro backdrop stated: India real GDP growth estimated at 7.6% for 2025-26, with the Reserve Bank of India projecting 6.9% real GDP growth for 2026-27; global growth is projected to moderate in 2026 and stabilise in 2027 with the balance of risks tilted to the downside (macro narrative routed via the profile prompt; repeated here only as the stated demand backdrop).
- Highest-ever order book of INR 1,24,000 Million reported for FY 2025-26 (source states INR 1,24,000 Million; equivalent to INR 12,400 crore).
- The Company ended FY 2025-26 with an order book providing full revenue visibility through FY 2027-28 and supporting a double-digit CAGR trajectory over the next three years.
- The order book is well diversified across businesses and geographies, with exports now representing over 14% of total order booking, compared to approximately 5% of revenue at IPO.
- New facilities in North and Western India are stated to support awarded programs across light vehicles, off-highway and tractor segments.
- Order-book-relevant wins disclosed during the year: entry into the hot end of the after-treatment system for a leading Japanese passenger vehicle OEM; a major clean air win with Europe's leading commercial truck manufacturer; a strategic win in the engine bearings business with a leading Japanese OEM in the last quarter; and adoption of the DaVinci DCx by a leading Indian OEM for a flagship SUV platform.
- A completed proof of concept on an after-treatment system for a leading European truck OEM to meet Euro VII legislation is described as indicating future export readiness (a capability proof point, not a stated order).

deepdive.thesis: Best-ever year for newly-listed Tenneco India: FY26 value-added-revenue (VAR) +12.3% to INR4,918 cr and record 18.8% EBITDA margin (up from 14.3% in FY24), debt-free with a standout 94% ROCE and a INR12,400 cr lifetime order book giving 100% visibility to its FY28 internal revenue target. The structural call is content-per-vehicle resilience through the EV slowdown (hybrids/ICE keep exhaust content, even raise it 1.5–2x) plus two disruptive growth vectors — the patented DaVinci DCx affordable mechanical suspension premiumizing India's PV ride quality, and a fast-scaling export book (China-plus-one + weak rupee + tech-equalization) lifting from ~5-6% of sales toward a 14-20% order-book share.

risks.note: The Company derives significant strategic and operational benefits from its association with the Tenneco Group through access to its technology platforms, intellectual property and operational processes. An adverse change in these arrangements or relationships could impact competitiveness, technology access, operational continuity and future growth visibility across businesses. Mitigation is close alignment with the Group across engineering, manufacturing and operational excellence, while strengthening local execution capability and localisation.
risks.risk: Dependence on the Tenneco Group and the risk of adverse changes in key relationships (strategic risk)

risks.note: A significant share of revenues comes from a limited number of OEM customers, so customer sourcing decisions, platform allocations, production schedules and commercial arrangements drive programme visibility. Changes in sourcing strategies, production volumes, pricing arrangements or platform mix by key customers may impact revenue concentration, operating performance and medium-term growth visibility. Mitigation is customer stickiness via early lifecycle engagement, a technology-intensive portfolio with rigorous validation and long programme lifecycles, and expansion across domestic and export programmes. The social capital section separately acknowledges customer concentration and supply-chain reliance as inherent stakeholder-dependency risks.
risks.risk: Revenue concentration across top customers (strategic risk)

risks.note: A significant portion of revenues is linked to PV and CV segments, whose demand depends on economic activity, infrastructure spending, freight movement, fuel prices, financing availability and consumer sentiment. A prolonged slowdown in vehicle production or lower industry demand could impact revenues, operating leverage and profitability. Mitigation is portfolio diversification across Clean Air, Champion Ignition, Powertrain and Advanced Ride Technologies, plus increasing participation in industrial and off-highway platforms and export programmes.
risks.risk: Revenue concentration in the passenger vehicle and commercial vehicle segments (strategic risk)

risks.note: OEM production schedules and order volumes are based on customer forecasts and market demand, so order visibility is subject to changes in production schedules, inventory levels and industry demand. The absence of firm long-term volume commitments may impact production planning, capacity utilisation, inventory management and operational efficiency across facilities. Mitigation is operational flexibility from a diversified programme portfolio and disciplined capacity planning, and closer work with customers on forecasting visibility. This is a structural qualifier on the disclosed order book.
risks.risk: Lack of firm volume commitments from customers (operational risk)

risks.note: Demand for several products, particularly Clean Air and emission-control systems, is linked to evolving emission regulations and compliance requirements. Delays, modifications or changes in emission standards and implementation timelines could influence product demand, programme timing, investment cycles and technology adoption across vehicle platforms. Mitigation is aligning engineering, product development and manufacturing readiness with evolving emission norms while leveraging global technology platforms and localisation. The MD&A separately notes that lower-horsepower (<75 Hp) tractor engine emission regulations were deferred to 2032, an example of exactly this timing risk crystallising.
risks.risk: Dependence on government emission standards and their implementation timelines (technological / regulatory risk)

risks.note: The Company is exposed to fluctuations in prices and availability of key raw materials and components including steel, precious metals and commodity-linked inputs. Sustained commodity price increases and supply bottlenecks across critical materials may impact margins, production continuity, working capital requirements and cost competitiveness. Mitigation is supplier diversification, strategic sourcing, inventory planning, cost optimisation and customer pass-through arrangements where applicable, supported by localisation.
risks.risk: Raw material price and availability risk, including steel and precious metals (operational risk)

risks.note: Geopolitical uncertainty, trade restrictions, tariff actions, regional conflicts and supply-chain realignments may affect raw material availability, energy costs and reliability, logistics networks, exports, commodity prices and customer production schedules. Sustained disruption may influence sourcing continuity, input costs, export competitiveness and demand visibility; changes in trade regulations and tariff structures may also affect cross-border supply chains and intercompany operations. Mitigation includes localisation, diversified supplier relationships, disciplined inventory planning, operational flexibility, diversification of energy sources and energy efficiency initiatives.
risks.risk: Dynamic geopolitical conditions, trade restrictions and tariff actions (strategic risk)

risks.note: Dependence on supplier networks is critical for uninterrupted production; disruptions from supplier instability may affect production timelines and lead to cost escalations. Mitigation is robust sourcing practices, comprehensive supplier qualification and review frameworks, diversified and dual-sourced procurement, supplier localisation, continuous engagement and transparent governance.
risks.risk: Supply chain dependence and supplier instability (BRSR material issue)

meta.thesis: Best-ever year for newly-listed Tenneco India: FY26 value-added-revenue (VAR) +12.3% to INR4,918 cr and record 18.8% EBITDA margin (up from 14.3% in FY24), debt-free with a standout 94% ROCE and a INR12,400 cr lifetime order book giving 100% visibility to its FY28 internal revenue target. The structural call is content-per-vehicle resilience through the EV slowdown (hybrids/ICE keep exhaust content, even raise it 1.5–2x) plus two disruptive growth vectors — the patented DaVinci DCx affordable mechanical suspension premiumizing India's PV ride quality, and a fast-scaling export book (China-plus-one + weak rupee + tech-equalization) lifting from ~5-6% of sales toward a 14-20% order-book share.
